message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 1900409 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_REFERENCE_ALREADY_EXISTS, 1900500 FAILED_TO_CREATE_VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT, 10503 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_CREATE_TIMEOUT (retry).

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: send X-Idempotency-Key on this POST. Docs (Idempotency): "For all `POST` endpoints, include an idempotency key in the request header (`X-Idempotency-Key`)." The API reference marks it optional; the headers guide lists it under 'Mandatory API Headers'. A reused key replays the first response ("the response will include the header `X-Idempotency-Cache-Hit: true`"), so reuse the key when retrying the same operation and use a new one for a new operation. X-Trace-Id is optional. For both: "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters." "Its length should be between 12 and 255 characters." The idempotency page also says "We recommend using a **UUID** string as your idempotency key": strip the UUID's hyphens to satisfy both.

Docs (Pay With Bank Transfer): "PWBT is currently available for transactions in **NGN** (Nigerian Naira) and **GHS** (Ghanaian Cedi) only." The API's currency enum is wider (NGN, GHS, EGP, KES, MAD, ZAR; customer_account_number is "required for EGP and KES").
Required: customer_id, reference, currency, account_type. Static: "You must set `amount` to `0` when creating a static virtual account." "Static accounts are valid for  `1000 years`".

Dynamic: expiry is an integer number of seconds (60-31536000). "You must define an expiry when creating a dynamic account." but the same page gives "Default (if not specified): 1 hour (3600 seconds)". "Do **not** allow customers to save dynamic account details."

Static NGN accounts: "For NGN virtual accounts, either of the following is required:" bvn or nin (11 digits); this sits under the static-account section and the guide's dynamic NGN example sends neither.

Show the customer data.amount, not the amount you sent: the guide's dynamic example requests 1500 and gets back 1530; "Transfer the exact amount to the provided virtual account details." Sandbox: X-Scenario-Key issuer:approved or issuer:failed simulates the incoming transfer.

Payment confirmation: Docs (Pay With Bank Transfer): "Flutterwave sends a `charge.completed` webhook to your configured webhook URL." Verify with get_charge (data.id from the webhook) and list payments with list_charges?virtual_account_id=….

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 1900409 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_REFERENCE_ALREADY_EXISTS, 1900500 FAILED_TO_CREATE_VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT, 10503 VIRTUAL_ACCOUNT_CREATE_TIMEOUT (retry). Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
